findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: The goroutines in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection call `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` on the incoming request `ctx`. The request context is cancelled as soon as the HTTP handler returns, which happens right after `Create` returns the response. The goroutine then runs the legacy SQL write with an already-cancelled context, so the 10s timeout never applies and the write can fail with `context canceled`. The failure is only recorded as a legacy error metric. This defeats the stated purpose of keeping legacy in sync. Detach cancellation while keeping values (user identity, namespace) with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Storage failure in Create is recorded as a legacy duration
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. The failed call was to unified storage, so the error is attributed to the legacy metric. Storage error rates are under-reported and legacy error rates are inflated. It should be `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: Storage failure in Update is recorded as a legacy duration
findings.body: The error path after `d.Storage.Update` calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `startStorage`. This is the same wrong-metric mistake as in Create: unified-storage update failures show up as legacy failures. It should be `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded with the storage metric
findings.body: Inside the async goroutine, the result of `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy)`. The legacy timing and errors are therefore mixed into the storage metrics, and the legacy metric is never emitted for this method. It should be `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses the object name as the kind label
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. Successful deletes are therefore labelled with the resource name. This creates one label value per deleted object (unbounded cardinality) and splits success and error series for the same operation.

findings.title: Delete stores the base logger in the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` should use the `log` variable built one line earlier. As written, the name, kind and method values are dropped from logs emitted by the storage layer and by the async legacy delete. Every other method uses `log`.

findings.title: Legacy Update re-applies the original objInfo instead of the object written to storage
findings.body: The previous implementation computed the updated object and wrapped it with `updateWrapper`, so legacy received the exact object that unified storage persisted. The new code passes the raw `objInfo` to `d.Legacy.Update` in a goroutine. For PATCH and PUT with a resourceVersion, `UpdatedObject` is evaluated again against the legacy store's own current object. Legacy and unified resourceVersions differ, so this can fail with a conflict or produce a different result. The two stores can then silently diverge, and the only trace is a legacy error metric.

findings.title: Tests never verify the async legacy write or its failure behavior
findings.body: Every Mode3 test asserts only the storage result. None waits for the goroutine or asserts that Legacy was called with the expected arguments. Nothing checks that a legacy error leaves the response unaffected. The legacy and storage mocks share one `mock.Mock`, so a storage expectation silently satisfies the legacy call. The legacy mock set up in the 'error' Create case is never used. A goroutine can also touch the mock after the test returns. As a result the core feature of this PR (async legacy write after a unified-storage write) is untested, and the bugs in the goroutines (context cancellation, wrong metrics) go undetected.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests read legacy state right after k8s writes, but legacy is written asynchronously
findings.body: `doPlaylistTests` creates and updates playlists through the k8s API and immediately compares them with the legacy `/api/playlists` endpoints via `getFromBothAPIs` and the legacy list. In mode 3 the legacy write is fire-and-forget, and with the request-context cancellation issue it may not happen at all. These new mode 3 subtests (file and unified) are therefore timing-dependent and can be flaky. They do not actually verify that legacy was updated.

findings.title: Unrelated go.work.sum churn including a duplicated entry
findings.body: The diff adds `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod` directly after an identical existing line, so it now appears twice. Together with the other added otel, genproto and alertmanager hashes, these changes are unrelated to the dual-writer feature and look like accidental output from a local `go work sync`. They should be dropped or regenerated cleanly.
